purpose: CAL experiment C1: count hidden_hostcall_buffer across every shipped device code object in two ROCm containers, gfx1100 and 21 other targets. CPU only, no GPU, no lease.
host: VM 101 (the VFIO guest), scanned inside docker containers, GPUs untouched

rocm714.note: this is the image the Radeon pair actually serves from

rocm10.note: same RCCL version string as the 7.14 arm, different binary and 33 more kernels; the version string is not an identifier

tools.clang-offload-bundler: same prefix, --list / --unbundle; required for CCOB (compressed) bundles
tools.librocm_kpack.so.0: site-packages/_rocm_sdk_core/lib/, AMD's own KPAK reader, driven from Python by ctypes

files.rocm714-gfx1100.jsonl: full scan, ROCm 7.14 arm, target gfx1100
files.rocm10-gfx1100.jsonl: full scan, ROCm 10.0 arm, target gfx1100
files.crossarch-rccl-rocm714.jsonl: RCCL kpack, every architecture it ships (20); hostcall_names is the complete list per target, with its md5
files.crossarch-rccl-rocm10.jsonl: RCCL kpack, every architecture it ships (21); same digest as the 7.14 arm on all 41 target-and-version pairs
files.crossarch-torch-rocm714.jsonl: torch kpack, every architecture it ships (24); hostcall_names_complete is false where an image's own five-name cap bit
files.crossarch-torch-rocm10.jsonl: torch kpack, every architecture it ships (25)

reruns: the four cross-architecture scans were run twice, 2026-09-04, in independent container instances of the same two images; every kernels/hostcall_kernels/binaries cell reproduced. The committed files are the second run, which also records the whole name list.
